newsitem.title: UK: Business panel slams UK on competition - paper.
newsitem.headline: Business panel slams UK on competition - paper.

text.p: The British government's record on promoting competition is described as confusing, weak and excessively political in a report by senior businessmen and academics, the Financial times said on Thursday.
The Commission on Public Policy and British business was set up under the auspices of the Institute for Public Policy Research, a think-tank with close links to the opposition Labour party.

The report, which is expected to be highly influential with Labour on its industrial policy, gives muted support for the implementation of the European Union's social chapter in Britain, said the newspaper.

The report said a national minimum wage could have benefits for "good employers" so long as it was not set too high but rejected Labour proposals to set up barriers to takeovers and create a super authority on competition.

The Commission's members included George Simpson, managing director of GEC, Bob Bauman, chairman of British Aerospace, Sir Christopher Hardy, chairman of Legal & General, and David Sainsbury of J. Sainsbury.
